sessions.startConfirm: This creates the organisation '{0}' on the git server, pushes the template folder into a template repository, and copies it into one repository per competitor. Existing repositories are left alone.
sessions.started: Session started. {0} competitor repositories are ready in '{1}'.
sessions.startFailed: Provisioning stopped: {0} — fix the cause and start the session again; competitors already provisioned are kept.
sessions.started.databases: {0} competitors got their own database, derived from the base name '{1}'.
sessions.startedPartially: Session started with {0} repositories ready and {1} steps failed: {2}. Fix the cause and start it again to retry only those.
sessions.startedSkipped: {0} competitors were skipped because they have no account on the git server: {1}. Provision their git accounts on the Competitors page, then start the session again to give them a repository.
sessions.startedSkippedDatabase: {0} competitors were granted no database access because they have no login on the SQL server: {1}. Provision their accounts on the Competitors page, then start the session again to grant them access.
sessions.stopConfirm: This stops the session accepting pushes, takes every competitor's access to their repository away and stops the session's docker services. Nothing is deleted: the repositories, their history and the competitors' database access are all kept, and starting the session again restores everything.
sessions.stopped: Session stopped. Repository access revoked for {0} competitors and {1} docker services stopped.
sessions.stoppedPartially: Session stopped with {0} steps failed: {1}. Fix the cause, then start and stop the session again to retry.
sessions.stopFailed: Stopping did not finish: {0} — the session no longer accepts pushes; fix the cause and stop it again to withdraw the rest.
sessions.closeServicesFailed: The session is closed, but its service containers could not be removed: {0}. They are still running on the docker host — remove them there, or close the session again once docker is reachable.
sessions.markingStarted: Marking is up: {0} containers running for '{1}', reachable from {2}. The list above says where to connect.
sessions.markingSkippedDatabase: The database-backed services were not started for '{0}': the SQL server holds no login for them, so no session database of theirs was ever created.
sessions.markingFailed: Starting marking did not finish: {0} — fix the cause and start marking again; containers already running are kept.
sessions.markingStopFailed: The marking containers could not be removed: {0}. They are still running on the docker host — remove them there, or stop marking again once docker is reachable.
sessions.progress.preparing: Preparing git organisation and starter template…
sessions.help.statusReadOnly: Use Start, Stop or Close on the sessions list — those provision repositories, grant and revoke access and cancel runs; setting the status alone does none of it.
sessions.help.slug: URL-safe identifier — lowercase letters, numbers and dashes.
sessions.help.templateFolder: Path the application container can read, copied into every competitor repository when the session is started. Required to start a session. Packages uploaded on the Starter packages page are offered here as /starter-packages/<name>/competitor-start.
sessions.help.description: Provide competition requirements and guidelines in markdown format.
sessions.help.judgementImage: Registered docker images plus every container package found in the Gitea registry. Type to filter, or enter any reference the judge host can pull. Leave empty for a session that is marked by hand: it still provisions repositories, databases and services, but no push is judged and no webhook is installed.
sessions.images.registryUnavailable: Registry images are not listed, so only registered images are offered. {0}
sessions.help.gitCredential: Used to `git clone` competitor submissions when a webhook arrives.
sessions.help.judgementImagePullCredenti: Used to `docker login` before pulling the judgement image, and the session's own service images, from a private registry.
sessions.help.databaseName: Not a database on its own: each competitor gets one of their own, named '<base>-<username>' — base 'session-1' gives 'session-1-joe-doe' and 'session-1-john-doe'. Only that competitor is granted access to theirs, so nobody can reach anybody else's work. Leave empty for a session with no database.
sessions.help.databaseAccess: Applied to every competitor inside their own database, and re-applied on each start — unticking a box and starting the session again takes the access away.
sessions.help.databaseSeedScript: A .sql file from the starter packages volume, run once against each competitor's database, at the moment starting the session creates it. A database that already exists is never reseeded — drop it and start the session again to run the script over. Every competitor is seeded from the same script, so they all start from identical data.
sessions.dockerImages.empty: No docker images configured for this session yet.
sessions.placeholders.rule: Every competitor gets their own copy of every service — their own container, their own host ports counted up from the ones you type, and their own settings — exactly as they each get their own session database. Placeholders are how the settings differ between them; a service using none still runs once per competitor, with identical settings.
sessions.placeholders.applyTo: Substituted in environment values, label values and volume host paths. Not in keys, not in container paths and not in the image reference. Write {{{{ for a literal '{{'.
sessions.placeholders.legend: Grey: same for everybody. Blue: this competitor — their mobile address is empty when they have none. Purple: this competitor's session database — while marking, these connect as the database administrator instead, and a competitor with no SQL login gets no copy of such a service.

sessions.marking.title: Marking
sessions.marking.oneAtATime: One competitor at a time per marking computer. The proxy sends this computer's requests to whichever competitor's container was started for its address, so stop the previous competitor's marking before pointing the same computer at another one.
sessions.help.markingIpAddress: The address of the computer you will be marking from — not the competitor's workstation, which is shown next to their name. It is the only address allowed through to their containers.
sessions.marking.noCompetitors: No competitor is enrolled in this session, so there is nothing to mark.
sessions.help.dockerImageDomain: Optional hostname the reverse proxy routes to this service, such as 'shop.skills.local' — a bare lowercase name, no http:// and no port. Every competitor uses the same address and reaches their OWN container, because the proxy matches on their workstation's IP. Set the container port beside it; port mappings stay optional and are not needed for routing. No two services of a session may share a domain.
sessions.help.dockerImageRoutedPort: The port the application listens on INSIDE the container — 8080 for most web images, 80 for nginx. The reverse proxy talks to it over the docker network, so a routed service needs no port mapping at all. Required when a domain is set, and must be empty without one.
mySession.service.urlHelp: Open this from your own workstation. The same address on any other machine leads to that competitor's container, not yours.
competitors.help.mobileIpAddress: Optional. The address of a phone or tablet the competitor was handed. It counts as the same competitor everywhere: it signs them in, and it reaches their own service containers during the competition and while their work is being marked. Must differ from the workstation address.
